title: Requisition list loads with pagination and four states
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.VIEW. At least 26 requisitions exist for the active company so page 2 is available.
steps:
1. Login as PURCHASE_OFFICER.
2. Navigate to /admin/purchase-requisitions.
3. Confirm loading state appears then resolves to table.
4. Verify paginator shows FIRST, PREVIOUS, page numbers, NEXT, LAST.
5. Click NEXT; confirm page 2 loads.
6. Apply status filter = DRAFT; confirm rows narrow.
testData: Company: Acme Trading Ltd. 26+ seeded requisitions.
expected: Table lists requisitions with requisition number, status badge, required-by date. Meta includes page/size/totalElements/totalPages/hasNext. HTTP 200.

title: Create requisition with GOODS line lands in DRAFT status
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.CREATE. At least one active GOODS product and unit of measure exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/purchase-requisitions/create.
2. Set required-by date and optional notes.
3. Add a line: choose product by name via picker; choose unit BAG; enter requestedQty=10, estimatedUnitCost=5000.
4. Submit.
testData: Product: Cement 50kg. Unit: BAG. requestedQty: 10. estimatedUnitCost: 5000.
expected: HTTP 201. Requisition status = DRAFT. Redirect to detail. uid appears only in the URL, not in any visible label.

title: Submit requisition transitions DRAFT to SUBMITTED
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.CREATE. A DRAFT requisition exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT requisition detail.
2. Click Submit.
3. Observe status badge updates.
testData: A DRAFT requisition created in P2P-002.
expected: Status changes to SUBMITTED. submittedAt is set and displayed. Submit button is hidden afterwards.

title: Approve a SUBMITTED requisition transitions to APPROVED
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. A SUBMITTED requisition exists.
steps:
1. Open the SUBMITTED requisition detail.
2. Click Approve.
3. Observe status badge.
expected: Status changes to APPROVED. approvedAt is set. Convert action is now offered.

title: Reject a SUBMITTED requisition with required reason
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. A SUBMITTED requisition exists.
steps:
1. Open the SUBMITTED requisition detail.
2. Click Reject.
3. Enter reason: Budget exceeded for Q2.
4. Confirm.
expected: Status changes to REJECTED. rejectedAt is set. Reason captured. Empty reason is blocked by the UI (Rejection reason is required).

title: Convert APPROVED requisition to Purchase Order
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. An APPROVED requisition with GOODS lines exists.
steps:
1. Open the APPROVED requisition detail.
2. Open Convert form; select target = Purchase Order.
3. Confirm.
expected: Returns created PO uid. Requisition status changes to CONVERTED with convertedToType=PURCHASE_ORDER. A View created PURCHASE_ORDER link routes to /admin/purchase-orders/uid/{uid}. uid is only in the link URL.

title: Convert APPROVED requisition to RFQ
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. An APPROVED requisition exists.
steps:
1. Open the APPROVED requisition detail.
2. Open Convert form; select target = RFQ.
3. Confirm.
expected: Created RFQ uid returned. Requisition status = CONVERTED, convertedToType = RFQ. Follow link routes to /admin/rfqs/uid/{uid}.

title: Cancel a non-final requisition
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.CREATE. A DRAFT or SUBMITTED requisition exists.
steps:
1. Open requisition detail.
2. Click Cancel.
3. Optionally enter a reason; confirm.
expected: Status changes to CANCELLED. cancelledAt is set.

title: Illegal requisition transitions are rejected
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. Requisitions in CONVERTED and CANCELLED states exist.
steps:
1. Attempt to submit an already-SUBMITTED requisition.
2. Attempt to approve a DRAFT (not submitted) requisition.
3. Attempt to cancel a CONVERTED requisition.
4. Attempt to convert a DRAFT requisition.
testData: One requisition in each relevant state.
expected: Each attempt is rejected with an error. Status does not change. Appropriate action buttons are hidden in the UI for terminal/invalid states.

title: PURCHASE.REQUISITION.CREATE user cannot approve
preconditions: A user with PURCHASE.REQUISITION.CREATE but NOT PURCHASE.REQUISITION.APPROVE. A SUBMITTED requisition exists.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open the SUBMITTED requisition detail.
3. Observe the Approve button.
expected: Approve button is hidden. Direct POST to /api/v1/purchase-requisitions/uid/{uid}/approve returns HTTP 403.

title: Cross-tenant requisition access returns forbidden state
preconditions: A requisition belonging to Company A. User belongs only to Company B.
steps:
1. Login as Company B user.
2. Navigate directly to the Company A requisition uid URL.
expected: API returns 403. The detail component shows the forbidden state (visually distinct from the loading, empty, and error states).

title: Create RFQ with supplier invites and GOODS lines (rootadmin only — RBAC defect)
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. PURCHASE.RFQ.CREATE is NOT seeded so only rootadmin can reach this endpoint. At least 2 active suppliers and 1 GOODS product exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/rfqs/create.
2. Set response-due date and notes.
3. Invite suppliers: choose each by name via picker (at least 2).
4. Add line: product by name, unit, quantity=100.
5. Submit.
testData: Suppliers: MegaSupply Co, BuildMart. Product: Cement 50kg. qty: 100.
expected: HTTP 201. RFQ status = DRAFT. Invited supplier names visible in the detail. Redirect to detail. uid only in URL.

title: Send RFQ transitions DRAFT to SENT
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. A DRAFT RFQ with invited suppliers exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT RFQ detail.
2. Click Send.
expected: Status badge changes to SENT. Success toast: Suppliers have been notified.

title: Capture two supplier quotes against a SENT RFQ
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. A SENT RFQ with at least 2 invited suppliers exists.
steps:
1. Open the SENT RFQ detail; click Capture Quote.
2. Pick first supplier by name; enter quotedQty and unitPrice=4800; submit.
3. Repeat for second supplier with unitPrice=4950.
testData: Supplier A unit price: 4800. Supplier B unit price: 4950.
expected: Each quote created with status RECEIVED. RFQ status becomes QUOTES_RECEIVED. Quotes listed in the RFQ quotes panel by supplier name.

title: Award RFQ to the winning quote — creates PO, marks other quotes NOT_AWARDED
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. An RFQ with at least 2 RECEIVED quotes exists.
steps:
1. In the quotes panel, click Award on the cheaper quote (supplier A at 4800).
2. Confirm the action.
testData: Winning quote: supplier A at unit price 4800.
expected: RFQ status changes to AWARDED. awardedPoUid returned and surfaced as a follow-link to /admin/purchase-orders/uid/{uid}. Winning quote status = AWARDED. Losing quote status = NOT_AWARDED. PO created in DRAFT.

title: RFQ create/send/award denied to a fully-granted custom role (RBAC seed defect)
preconditions: A custom role granted every available (seeded) permission. A SENT RFQ exists.
steps:
1. Login as the custom-role user.
2. Attempt to navigate to /admin/rfqs/create.
3. On the SENT RFQ, attempt to capture a quote and award.
testData: Custom role with all seeded permissions.
expected: Create route guard blocks (PURCHASE.RFQ.CREATE not grantable). Award and capture-quote buttons are hidden. Any direct API call returns 403. Only rootadmin succeeds.

title: PO list loads with search, pagination, and four states
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.VIEW. At least 26 POs exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/purchase-orders.
2. Enter a search term in the q field.
3. Page through with paginator controls.
expected: List shows order number, status badge, supplier name, order total. q filters results. Paginator shows all five controls. Money formatted as CUR 1,234.56.

title: Add, edit, and remove a line on a DRAFT PO
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.CREATE and PURCHASE.ORDER.VIEW. A DRAFT PO exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT PO detail.
2. Add a line: search product by name via picker; choose unit; orderedQty=20; unitCost=4800.
3. Edit the line qty to 25.
4. Remove the line.
testData: Product: Cement 50kg. Unit: BAG. qty: 20, then 25. unitCost: 4800.
expected: Line added (201), edited (200), removed (204). PO orderTotalAmount recomputed server-side after each change. Product and unit chosen by name only.

title: Place a PO transitions DRAFT to ORDERED
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.CREATE. A DRAFT PO with at least one line exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT PO detail.
2. Click Place.
expected: Status changes to ORDERED. Human-readable orderNumber (PO-####) is assigned and displayed. orderedAt is set. Receive, Close, and Void actions become available.

title: Void a PO with required reason
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.VOID. A DRAFT and an ORDERED PO exist.
steps:
1. Open the ORDERED PO detail.
2. Click Void.
3. Enter reason: Supplier discontinued item.
4. Confirm.
expected: Status changes to VOID. voidedAt and voidReason are set. Empty reason is blocked by the UI (A void reason is required).

title: Close a PO from ORDERED, PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, and RECEIVED states
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.CREATE. One PO in ORDERED state and one in RECEIVED state exist.
steps:
1. Open the ORDERED PO; click Close.
2. Repeat for the RECEIVED PO.
testData: One ORDERED PO, one RECEIVED PO.
expected: Status changes to CLOSED in both cases. closedAt is set. PO becomes read-only.

title: Void blocked for CLOSED PO; line edits blocked for non-DRAFT PO
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.ORDER.VOID and PURCHASE.ORDER.CREATE. A CLOSED PO and an ORDERED PO exist.
steps:
1. Attempt to void the CLOSED PO.
2. Attempt to add a line to the ORDERED PO.
expected: Void on CLOSED PO is rejected (only DRAFT/ORDERED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED voidable). Line add on ORDERED PO is rejected (DRAFT-only). Both return error messages without changing the status.

title: PURCHASE_OFFICER without VOID cannot void a PO
preconditions: A user with PURCHASE.ORDER.CREATE but not PURCHASE.ORDER.VOID. An ORDERED PO exists.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open the ORDERED PO detail.
3. Observe the Void button.
expected: Void button is hidden. Direct POST to void endpoint returns HTTP 403.

title: Partial goods receipt then receive-remaining — PO transitions ORDERED > PARTIALLY_RECEIVED > RECEIVED
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.RECEIVE. An ORDERED PO with GOODS lines (outstanding qty=20) exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/goods-receipts/create.
2. Choose the PO by order number via picker.
3. Receive partial qty=12; submit.
4. Create a second GR for the remaining qty=8; submit.
testData: PO outstanding qty: 20. First receipt: 12. Second receipt: 8.
expected: First GR is RECEIVED (GRN-#### assigned). PO status = PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. Second GR is RECEIVED. PO status = RECEIVED. Stock increased by 20 units total.

title: Over-receipt is rejected
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.RECEIVE. An ORDERED PO with 20 outstanding units exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/goods-receipts/create.
2. Choose the PO by order number.
3. Enter receivedQty=25 (exceeds outstanding).
4. Submit.
expected: Service rejects with an error (BR-PURCH-10: over-receipt). GR is not created. PO status unchanged.

title: GR against a DRAFT or VOID PO is rejected
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.RECEIVE. A DRAFT PO and a VOID PO exist.
steps:
1. Attempt to create a GR selecting the DRAFT PO.
2. Attempt to create a GR selecting the VOID PO.
expected: Both attempts are rejected. GR is not created. Error message is returned without leaking internal details.

title: Void a RECEIVED GR reverses stock and restores PO outstanding (API-level)
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.VOID. A RECEIVED GR exists with associated stock movements.
steps: 1. Call POST /api/v1/goods-receipts/uid/{uid}/void with VoidGoodsReceiptRequest body.
expected: GR status changes to VOID. Emits STOCK.RECEIPT.VOIDED event. PO outstanding qty is restored. Stock movement is reversed (append-only reversal, not deletion).

title: Create landed cost with basis BY_VALUE over a RECEIVED GR (rootadmin only — RBAC defect)
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. PURCHASE.LANDED_COST.CREATE is NOT seeded (controller uses underscore; seed uses LANDEDCOST without underscore). At least one RECEIVED GR with GOODS lines exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/landed-costs/create.
2. Select basis = By Value.
3. Choose GR by GRN number via picker.
4. Add charge FREIGHT=200000.
5. Add charge DUTY=150000.
6. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. LC status = DRAFT. Charges captured. Basis = BY_VALUE.

title: Create landed cost with basis BY_QUANTITY and all five charge types
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. A RECEIVED GR exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/landed-costs/create.
2. Select basis = By Quantity.
3. Choose GR by GRN number.
4. Add one charge of each type: FREIGHT, DUTY, CLEARING, INSURANCE, OTHER.
5. Submit.
testData: Basis: BY_QUANTITY. One charge per LandedCostChargeType.
expected: HTTP 201. LC status = DRAFT. All five charge types captured. Allocation will be pro-rata to qty_in_base on confirm.

title: Confirm landed cost allocates charges to GR lines
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. A DRAFT LC over RECEIVED GR(s) exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT LC detail.
2. Click Confirm.
expected: LC status changes to CONFIRMED. Charges are allocated across GR lines per basis (BY_VALUE = pro-rata to line value; BY_QUANTITY = pro-rata to qty). LandedCostAllocated outbox event published.

title: Landed cost view/create/confirm denied to fully-granted custom role (RBAC seed defect)
preconditions: A custom role granted every seeded permission. A DRAFT LC exists.
steps:
1. Login as the custom-role user.
2. Navigate to /admin/landed-costs.
3. Attempt to create a new LC and confirm the existing DRAFT.
testData: Custom role with all seeded permissions.
expected: Nav item is hidden. Route guard redirects away. Any direct API call returns 403. Only rootadmin succeeds. This confirms the LANDEDCOST vs LANDED_COST permission code mismatch.

title: Enter supplier bill against PO — all lines match, bill status = MATCHED
preconditions: User has AP.BILL.ENTER and AP.BILL.MATCH. An ORDERED or RECEIVED PO and a matching GR (same qty and unit cost) exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/ap/supplier-bills/enter.
2. Pick supplier by name; enter supplier invoice no INV-2026-014, bill date, due date, currency TZS.
3. Choose the Purchase Order by number via picker.
4. Add bill lines matching GR qty=20 and unitCost=4800.
5. Click Enter Bill and Match.
testData: Invoice no: INV-2026-014. Currency: TZS. qty: 20. unitCost: 4800.
expected: Bill created DRAFT (HTTP 201). Match runs automatically. All lines matchStatus = MATCHED. Bill status = MATCHED. GL posts synchronously on full match. Result panel shows: All lines matched — bill is ready for payment.

title: Bill match produces HELD_PRICE_VARIANCE then accept-variance posts
preconditions: User has AP.BILL.ENTER and AP.BILL.MATCH. A PO and GR at unitCost=4800 exist.
steps:
1. Enter a bill with unitCost=5200 (over price tolerance).
2. Observe match result.
3. Click Accept Variance on the held line.
expected: Line matchStatus = HELD_PRICE_VARIANCE. Bill status = HELD. Price variance amount and percentage shown. After accepting, line status = VARIANCE_ACCEPTED. Once all variances accepted, bill status = MATCHED and GL posts.

title: Bill match produces HELD_QTY_VARIANCE
preconditions: User has AP.BILL.MATCH. A GR received qty=20 exists. A bill with qty=25 exists.
steps:
1. Enter a bill with line qty=25.
2. Run match.
expected: Line matchStatus = HELD_QTY_VARIANCE. Bill status = HELD. qtyVariance shown. Accepting the variance transitions to VARIANCE_ACCEPTED then MATCHED.

title: Service-only bill with no PO is entered without 3-way match
preconditions: User has AP.BILL.ENTER. A SERVICE supplier exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/ap/supplier-bills/enter.
2. Pick SERVICE supplier by name.
3. Enter invoice details and service lines.
4. Submit without choosing a PO.
expected: Bill created in DRAFT without triggering 3-way match. No stock movement. Running match on a no-PO bill is rejected or handled gracefully.

title: AP.VIEW-only user cannot enter a bill
preconditions: A user with AP.VIEW but not AP.BILL.ENTER.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Navigate to /admin/ap/supplier-bills.
3. Attempt to access the Enter Bill route.
expected: Enter Bill route and button are hidden. Direct POST to /api/v1/ap/supplier-bills returns HTTP 403.

title: Create purchase return (partial) against a RECEIVED GR
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.RETURN.CREATE. A RECEIVED GR with GOODS lines (received qty=20) exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/purchase-returns/create.
2. Choose the GR by GRN number via picker.
3. Enter reason: Damaged on arrival.
4. Enter returnedQty=5 for the line.
5. Submit.
testData: GRN selected. reason: Damaged on arrival. returnedQty: 5.
expected: HTTP 201. Purchase return status = DRAFT. Lines reference GR lines. Return number assigned.

title: Confirm purchase return — rootadmin only due to PURCHASE.RETURN.CONFIRM not seeded
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. A DRAFT purchase return exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT purchase return detail.
2. Click Confirm.
expected: Status changes to CONFIRMED. PURCHASE.RETURNED outbox event published (triggers stock-out and supplier debit downstream).

title: returnedQty exceeding received qty is rejected
preconditions: User has PURCHASE.RETURN.CREATE. A RECEIVED GR with received qty=20 exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/purchase-returns/create.
2. Choose the GR.
3. Enter returnedQty=25 for the line.
4. Submit.
expected: Service rejects the return. Error message returned. Return is not created.

title: View and edit purchase settings — rootadmin only due to RBAC seed defect
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. PURCHASE.SETTINGS.VIEW and PURCHASE.SETTINGS.EDIT are NOT seeded (controller uses VIEW/EDIT; seed only has MANAGE). A company exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/purchase-settings.
2. Toggle poApprovalEnabled = true.
3. Set threshold=1000000 and currency TZS.
4. Save.
expected: Settings persisted (HTTP 200). POs at or above threshold will subsequently enter PoApprovalStatus.PENDING.

title: Full P2P chain: requisition > RFQ > quote > award(PO) > place > receive > landed-cost > bill > match > return
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. One GOODS supplier, one GOODS product and unit, company with default branch, purchase settings with approval disabled.
steps:
1. Create requisition (DRAFT) with one GOODS line; Submit; Approve; Convert to RFQ.
2. Open RFQ; Send; Capture two quotes (different prices); Award the cheaper — PO created DRAFT.
3. Open PO; Place (ORDERED).
4. Create GR for full qty — PO becomes RECEIVED, GRN-#### assigned.
5. Create landed cost (BY_VALUE, FREIGHT charge) over the GR; Confirm.
6. Enter supplier bill matching PO qty and price; auto match — bill status = MATCHED.
7. Create purchase return for damaged units against the GR; Confirm.
testData: GOODS supplier. GOODS product. Approval disabled. Two quotes with different unit prices.
expected: Every transition lands the expected status: Requisition CONVERTED, RFQ AWARDED, Quote AWARDED/NOT_AWARDED, PO RECEIVED, GR RECEIVED, LC CONFIRMED, Bill MATCHED, Return CONFIRMED. All document numbers are human-readable (PO-####, GRN-####). uids appear only in URLs.
permission: rootadmin (full chain requires codes not grantable to custom roles)

title: Stock on-hand list loads with pagination and company/branch scope
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW. At least 25 GOODS products with on-hand rows at the active branch.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock.
2. Confirm table rows with quantity (3-dp), reorder level, and negative/low flags.
3. Verify paginator shows all five controls.
4. Click NEXT; confirm page 2 loads.
5. Click FIRST to return.
expected: Table shows product code/name, quantity (3-dp), reorder level, negative and low flags. ApiResponse with meta (page/size/totalElements/totalPages/hasNext). HTTP 200.

title: On-hand search filter with debounce resets to page 0
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW. Products including one named WIDGET-100 exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock; go to page 2.
2. Type WIDGET into the search box.
3. Wait for 300ms debounce.
4. Confirm the request fires with q=WIDGET&page=0.
expected: Results filtered to matching rows. Current page resets to 0. No uid visible in the table.

title: On-hand negative and low-stock derived flags are displayed
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW. One product with negative on-hand (oversold). One product with quantity at or below its reorderLevel.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock.
2. Locate the negative-on-hand row and the low-stock row.
testData: Product A: quantity < 0. Product B: quantity <= reorderLevel.
expected: negative=true row is visually flagged with an overselling indicator. low=true row is flagged with a reorder indicator. Both flags are server-derived from StockOnHandDto.from(), not stored columns.

title: NO-PERMISSION user cannot access stock on-hand
preconditions: A user with zero permissions assigned to a company/branch.
steps:
1. Login as the no-permission user.
2. Inspect the shell nav.
3. Attempt to navigate directly to /admin/stock.
expected: No Inventory nav items render. Direct navigation is redirected to /admin/home by the route guard (requirePermission('STOCK.VIEW')). Backend GET /api/v1/stock/on-hand returns 403.

title: By-Location view shows per-location on-hand rows
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW. Multiple stock locations at the active branch with on-hand.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock; select a branch.
2. Toggle view mode to By Location.
3. Confirm rows show location code/name, product code/name, quantity, onHandValue, avgCost, currency.
expected: LocationOnHandRowDto rows paged. Money formatted with currency. No raw uid visible. companyId and branchId sent as wire params.

title: By-Product view selects product via picker and lists all holding locations
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW. A GOODS product held at at least 2 locations.
steps:
1. Toggle to By Product.
2. Type product name in the search; pick result by name (code — name format).
3. Confirm per-location breakdown loads.
expected: All locations holding the product shown with quantity/value. productUid placed in URL path only; product chosen by name.

title: Manual positive adjustment with reason COUNT_CORRECTION
preconditions: User has STOCK.ADJUST. An on-hand row for a GOODS product exists.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock; on a row click Adjust.
2. Product is pre-selected by name. Choose reason = COUNT_CORRECTION.
3. Enter quantity=10, note=cycle count fix.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. StockMovementDto with movementType=ADJUSTMENT and direction=IN. On-hand increases by 10. Adjustment is an appended movement row (not an edit).

title: Manual negative adjustment with reason DAMAGE drives stock down
preconditions: User has STOCK.ADJUST. An on-hand row with quantity > 3 exists.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock; click Adjust on a row.
2. Choose reason = DAMAGE.
3. Enter quantity=-3.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. direction=OUT. On-hand decreases by 3. If this creates a negative on-hand, the negative flag is set (allowed but flagged — not a hard reject).

title: STOCK.VIEW-only user cannot perform manual adjustment
preconditions: A user with STOCK.VIEW but not STOCK.ADJUST.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open /admin/stock.
3. Observe the Adjust action on a row.
expected: Adjust action is hidden. Direct POST to /api/v1/stock/adjustments returns HTTP 403.

title: Opening balance for a never-tracked product
preconditions: User has STOCK.OPENING. A GOODS product with NO prior stock movement at the active branch.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock; click Opening balance.
2. Pick the product by name via picker.
3. Enter quantity=100, note=go-live.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. StockMovementDto with movementType=OPENING_BALANCE and direction=IN. On-hand becomes 100.

title: Opening balance rejected when stock is already tracked
preconditions: User has STOCK.OPENING. A product that already has an opening balance or prior movement.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock; click Opening balance.
2. Pick the already-tracked product.
3. Enter quantity=50.
4. Submit.
expected: Backend rejects (400/409). Inline error from errors[] array. On-hand unchanged.

title: Set reorder level then clear it
preconditions: User has STOCK.ADJUST. An on-hand row exists.
steps:
1. Click reorder-level edit on a row; enter 5; save.
2. Confirm the low flag is set if quantity<=5.
3. Edit again; clear the field; save.
expected: Returns updated StockOnHandDto. After setting 5, low=true when quantity<=5. After clearing, low=false. uid only in URL path.

title: Create stock location for each LocationType
preconditions: User has STOCK.LOCATION.MANAGE. At least one branch exists.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock/locations; click Create.
2. Enter code=WH-01, name=Main Warehouse, locationType=WAREHOUSE, pick branch by name.
3. Submit.
4. Repeat for STORE, VAN, QUARANTINE, OTHER.
testData: Types: WAREHOUSE, STORE, VAN, QUARANTINE, OTHER.
expected: HTTP 201 for each. StockLocationDto with status=ACTIVE and isDefault=false. Branch chosen by name via picker; code/name stored server-side.

title: Create location with makeDefault=true clears previous default
preconditions: User has STOCK.LOCATION.MANAGE. A branch already has a default location L1.
steps:
1. Create a new location L2 with the Make default checkbox ticked.
2. Reload the locations list.
expected: L2 isDefault=true. L1 isDefault=false. Only one location per branch carries isDefault=true.

title: Deactivate then reactivate a stock location
preconditions: User has STOCK.LOCATION.MANAGE. An ACTIVE non-default location exists.
steps:
1. On the location row click Deactivate; confirm.
2. Verify row shows INACTIVE.
3. Click Reactivate.
4. Verify row returns to ACTIVE.
expected: Status transitions ACTIVE > INACTIVE > ACTIVE. No hard deletion occurs (soft lifecycle). HTTP 204 on deactivate.

title: STOCK.LOCATION.VIEW-only user cannot create or edit locations
preconditions: A user with STOCK.LOCATION.VIEW only.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open /admin/stock/locations.
3. Observe Create and Edit actions.
expected: List renders. Create button and row edit controls are hidden. Direct POST returns 403.

title: Create IN_TRANSIT cross-branch transfer with two lines
preconditions: User has STOCK.TRANSFER.CREATE. At least 2 branches, each with an active location and stock.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock-transfers/create.
2. Pick source branch and location by name via pickers.
3. Pick destination branch and location by name.
4. Set transferDate; transferMode = IN_TRANSIT.
5. Add line 1: product by name, qty=5.
6. Add line 2: product by name, qty=2.
7. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. StockTransferDto with status=DRAFT and transferMode=IN_TRANSIT. transferNumber assigned. All source/dest/product selected by name only.

title: IN_TRANSIT transfer: DRAFT > DISPATCHED > RECEIVED full lifecycle
preconditions: Dispatch user has STOCK.TRANSFER.CREATE. Receive user has STOCK.TRANSFER.RECEIVE. A DRAFT IN_TRANSIT transfer exists.
steps:
1. On the DRAFT IN_TRANSIT transfer detail, click Dispatch (as CREATE holder).
2. Verify status = DISPATCHED and dispatchedAt is set. Source stock decreases.
3. As the RECEIVE-holder, click Receive.
4. Verify status = RECEIVED and receivedAt is set. Destination stock increases.
expected: Status transitions: DRAFT > DISPATCHED > RECEIVED. Stock moves between locations via TRANSFER_OUT and TRANSFER_IN events. Movements are appended, not edited.

title: INSTANT same-branch transfer completes in one step DRAFT > COMPLETED
preconditions: User has STOCK.TRANSFER.CREATE. Two active locations in the SAME branch with source stock.
steps:
1. Create a transfer with both locations in the same branch; transferMode = INSTANT.
2. On the DRAFT+INSTANT detail, click Complete instant.
expected: Status transitions from DRAFT to COMPLETED in one transaction. Stock moves immediately between locations with no in-transit state.

title: Cancel a DRAFT transfer — no stock movement
preconditions: User has STOCK.TRANSFER.CREATE. A DRAFT transfer exists.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT transfer detail.
2. Click Cancel; confirm.
expected: Status changes to CANCELLED. No stock movement occurred. HTTP 204.

title: Illegal transfer transitions are rejected
preconditions: User has relevant transfer permissions.
steps:
1. Attempt to receive a DRAFT (not dispatched) IN_TRANSIT transfer.
2. Attempt to dispatch an already-DISPATCHED transfer.
3. Attempt to complete-instant a DISPATCHED transfer.
4. Attempt to cancel a RECEIVED transfer.
5. Attempt to dispatch an INSTANT-mode transfer.
testData: Transfers in various states and modes.
expected: Each attempt is rejected with 400/409. Status does not change. FE never offers the invalid action button for the wrong state or mode.

title: STOCK.TRANSFER.VIEW-only user cannot create a transfer
preconditions: A user with STOCK.TRANSFER.VIEW only.
steps:
1. Login as the VIEW-only user.
2. Navigate to /admin/stock-transfers.
3. Attempt to navigate to /admin/stock-transfers/create.
expected: List renders. Route guard blocks /create. Direct POST returns 403.

title: Create FULL count — snapshots systemQty, enters COUNTING
preconditions: User has STOCK.COUNT.CREATE. An active location with on-hand across several GOODS products exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock-counts/create.
2. Select company, branch; pick location by name via uid picker.
3. countDate = today; countType = FULL.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. StockCountDto with status=COUNTING. frozenAt set. countNumber assigned. One line per on-hand product with systemQty snapshot.

title: Enter counted quantities and observe variance
preconditions: User has STOCK.COUNT.CREATE. A COUNTING count exists.
steps:
1. Open the count detail.
2. Line A: type countedQty=12 (system=10, variance=+2).
3. Line B: type countedQty=7 (system=9, variance=-2), reason=SHRINKAGE.
4. Click Enter / Save.
testData: Line A: counted=12, system=10. Line B: counted=7, system=9, reason=SHRINKAGE.
expected: Lines persist countedQty. varianceQty = countedQty - systemQty shown with directional colour. Document stays COUNTING.

title: Post a count — creates ADJUSTMENT movements and GL variance journal
preconditions: User has STOCK.COUNT.POST. A COUNTING count with at least one variance exists.
steps:
1. On the count detail, click Post.
2. Supply postingDate = 2026-06-14.
3. Confirm.
expected: Status changes to COUNTING > POSTED. postedAt set. Per varying line, a movementUid (ADJUSTMENT movement) and varianceValue assigned. One varianceGlEntryUid on the document. POSTED state is read-only.

title: COUNT.CREATE-only user cannot post a count
preconditions: A user with STOCK.COUNT.CREATE but not STOCK.COUNT.POST. A COUNTING count with variances exists.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open the COUNTING count detail.
3. Observe the Post button.
expected: Post button is hidden. Direct PATCH to post endpoint returns HTTP 403.

title: Cancel a COUNTING count — no GL posted
preconditions: User has STOCK.COUNT.CREATE. A COUNTING count exists.
steps:
1. Open the COUNTING count detail.
2. Click Cancel; confirm.
expected: Status changes to CANCELLED. No GL entries or stock movements posted. HTTP 204.

title: Illegal count transitions are rejected — re-post, cancel-after-post, enter-after-post
preconditions: A POSTED count and a CANCELLED count exist.
steps:
1. Attempt to post an already-POSTED count.
2. Attempt to enter quantities on a POSTED count.
3. Attempt to cancel a POSTED count.
4. Attempt to post a CANCELLED count.
expected: Each attempt returns 400/409. FE shows read-only (no action buttons) for POSTED and CANCELLED states.

title: Batch list by location and product (rootadmin only — STOCK.BATCH.VIEW not seeded)
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. STOCK.BATCH.VIEW is not seeded (V41 seeds INVENTORY.BATCH.VIEW; controller gates on STOCK.BATCH.VIEW). Batch records exist for a lot-tracked product.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock/batches.
2. Pick location by name via picker.
3. Pick product by name.
4. Observe batch rows.
expected: StockBatchDto rows paged showing lotNumber, manufactureDate, expiryDate, qtyOnHand, expired flag. Product and location selected by name only.
permission: STOCK.BATCH.VIEW (NOT seeded — rootadmin only; see DEFECT INV-901)

title: Expiring batches report with horizon date
preconditions: User has INVENTORY.EXPIRY.VIEW. Batches with qty>0 expiring before and after a horizon date exist.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock/batches; switch to Expiring Soon.
2. Default horizon = today+30; confirm batches expiring on or before the horizon (qty>0) are listed.
3. Change horizon date; confirm result set changes.
expected: Paged StockBatchDto expiring set. Already-expired rows flagged red. Near-expiry warned. Horizon change triggers a new filtered result.

title: DEFECT: ORG_ADMIN denied batch/serial access due to permission code mismatch
preconditions: ORG_ADMIN role (granted INVENTORY.BATCH.VIEW via V41). Non-superuser.
steps:
1. Login as ORG_ADMIN.
2. Navigate to /admin/stock/batches and /admin/stock/serials.
3. Observe nav items and page behaviour.
4. As rootadmin, navigate to the same screens.
expected: ORG_ADMIN: nav items for Batches and Serials are hidden (nav checks STOCK.BATCH.VIEW which is not granted). Direct API calls return 403. rootadmin: screens load successfully (superuser bypass). This is a known defect: V41 seeds INVENTORY.BATCH.VIEW; controllers gate on STOCK.BATCH.VIEW.

title: Serial list by location and product with status filter (rootadmin only)
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. Serial-tracked product with serials in each status (IN_STOCK, ISSUED, RETURNED) at a location.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock/serials (By Location mode).
2. Pick location and product via pickers.
3. Leave status blank — all serials shown.
4. Set status = IN_STOCK; observe filter.
5. Repeat for ISSUED and RETURNED.
expected: StockSerialDto rows with serialNumber, serialStatus badge, location. Status filter narrows correctly for each value.

title: Serial lookup by serial number — found and not-found states
preconditions: Run as rootadmin. Serial SN-0001 exists for a known product.
steps:
1. In /admin/stock/serials pick the product; type SN-0001; click Look up.
2. Confirm the matched serial card shows current status/location.
3. Look up SN-XXXX (non-existent).
testData: Known serial: SN-0001. Unknown serial: SN-XXXX.
expected: Found: single StockSerialDto displayed. Not found: 404 mapped to a distinct not-found UI state (separate from loading/error/forbidden).

title: Valuation report renders rows, total, and GL reconciliation — ties=true
preconditions: User has INVENTORY.VALUATION.VIEW. Valued on-hand rows exist whose total equals the GL 1300 Inventory balance.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock/valuation.
2. Confirm per-product rows (code/name, quantity, avgCost, inventory value).
3. Confirm the reconciliation bar shows GREEN Reconciled to GL when ties=true.
expected: StockValuationReportDto with rows, totalValue, recon {label, computed, expected, difference, ties=true}, currency. Money formatted as CUR 1,234.56.

title: Valuation recon mismatch (ties=false) shows finance alarm
preconditions: User has INVENTORY.VALUATION.VIEW. Stock-ledger vs GL drift created so Σ on_hand_value ≠ GL 1300.
steps:
1. Open /admin/stock/valuation.
2. Inspect the reconciliation bar.
expected: ties=false. RED finance-grade alarm shown. difference = computed - expected displayed. Mismatch is surfaced prominently, not hidden.

title: Set opening valuation for an unvalued on-hand row
preconditions: User has INVENTORY.OPENING.SET. An on-hand row with quantity>0 but avgCost=null exists (unvalued).
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/stock/valuation/opening.
2. Select the unvalued row by product label.
3. Enter openingCost=12.50.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. OpeningValuationResultDto (openingValue + currency). GL posts DR INVENTORY (1300) / CR OPENING_BALANCE_EQUITY (3100). Row disappears from the unvalued list.

title: Setting opening valuation on an already-valued row is rejected
preconditions: User has INVENTORY.OPENING.SET. An on-hand row already valued (avgCost set).
steps: 1. Attempt to set opening valuation on the already-valued row via direct API call or stale list.
expected: Backend returns 409. FE shows: already has an opening valuation set (one-time per on-hand row). on-hand value unchanged.

title: INVENTORY.VALUATION.VIEW-lacking user cannot see the valuation report
preconditions: A user without INVENTORY.VALUATION.VIEW.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Navigate to /admin/stock/valuation.
expected: Component canView=false; no fetch triggered. Backend GET returns 403. Nav item hidden.

title: Cross-tenant stock data is inaccessible
preconditions: Full inventory perms in Tenant B. Data in Tenant A and Tenant B.
steps:
1. Login as Tenant B user.
2. Attempt to read Tenant A on-hand, locations, transfers, counts, batches by deep-link uid.
3. Attempt to view Tenant A valuation report.
testData: Tenant A uids for various resources.
expected: Tenant A uids return 403 or 404 scoped to Tenant B. Valuation report scoped to Tenant B company via JWT principal. No Tenant A data leaks.
permission: Full inventory perms in Tenant B

title: Branch switching changes on-hand and count context
preconditions: User has STOCK.VIEW and STOCK.COUNT.VIEW. User assigned to many branches.
steps:
1. On /admin/stock, switch the branch selector to a non-default branch.
2. Confirm on-hand reloads for that branch.
3. Repeat on counts.
expected: Data follows the active branch. Default-branch and non-default-branch on-hand sets differ. User assigned to only one branch cannot switch to another (denied).

title: BOM list loads with company scope, status filter, and pagination
preconditions: User has BOM.VIEW. At least one BOM exists. BOMs in DRAFT, ACTIVE, and ARCHIVED statuses exist.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/boms.
2. Confirm table renders BOM rows with parent product name/code, version, status badge, output qty, yield %.
3. Select status filter = Draft; confirm only DRAFT BOMs shown.
4. Select Active, then Archived, then All.
5. Page through with paginator.
testData: Company: Acme Manufacturing. BOMs in all three statuses.
expected: Each filter re-queries with status= param and shows only matching rows. Paginator shows all five controls. No uid visible in any column.

title: Create BOM (DRAFT) via inline form using product picker
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. An ACTIVE GOODS product exists in the company.
steps:
1. On /admin/boms, click the create toggle.
2. In the parent product picker, search and select by name.
3. Enter outputQty=10, yieldPercent=95, notes=Pilot batch.
4. Submit.
expected: HTTP 201. New DRAFT row appears with versionNo. uid appears only in the success alert link, not in any visible cell. Parent product shown by name.

title: Add components to a DRAFT BOM — Auto, MAKE, and BUY sourcing
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. A DRAFT BOM exists. Active component products exist.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT BOM detail; click Add component.
2. Select component product by name via picker.
3. Enter qtyPer=2, scrapPercent=5, reference=RES-1; sourcing=Auto.
4. Submit. Repeat with MAKE and BUY sourcing.
testData: qtyPer: 2. scrapPercent: 5. reference: RES-1. Sourcing: Auto, MAKE, BUY.
expected: HTTP 201 for each. Component line appended with line number, component code/name, qty per, sourcing, scrap %. With Auto sourcing, server derives MAKE if child has an ACTIVE BOM else BUY.

title: Edit and remove BOM component on DRAFT BOM
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. A DRAFT BOM with at least 2 components.
steps:
1. Click edit on a component; change qtyPer=3.5, sourcing=BUY, scrapPercent=0; save.
2. Click remove on another component; confirm.
expected: Edit returns updated component (200). Remove returns 204 and line disappears. Only DRAFT BOMs allow structural changes (edit/remove hidden on ACTIVE BOMs in UI).

title: Activate DRAFT BOM — transitions to ACTIVE with effective-from date
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. A DRAFT BOM with at least one valid component exists. No prior ACTIVE version.
steps:
1. Open the DRAFT BOM detail.
2. Click Activate.
3. Enter effectiveFrom = today.
4. Confirm.
expected: Status changes to ACTIVE. effectiveFrom set, effectiveTo null, activatedAt stamped. Success: BOM activated.

title: Activating a new version supersedes the prior ACTIVE BOM (one-active rule)
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. Product has ACTIVE BOM v1 and DRAFT BOM v2 (same parent).
steps:
1. Open DRAFT v2.
2. Click Activate with effectiveFrom = today.
testData: ACTIVE BOM v1, DRAFT BOM v2 for same parent product.
expected: v2 becomes ACTIVE (effectiveTo null). v1 atomically becomes ARCHIVED with effectiveTo = effectiveFrom and archivedAt stamped. Only one ACTIVE BOM remains for the parent. v1 is archived not deleted.

title: Archive a BOM — DRAFT or ACTIVE transitions to ARCHIVED
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. An ACTIVE BOM and a DRAFT BOM exist.
steps:
1. Open the ACTIVE BOM detail; click Archive; confirm.
2. Repeat for the DRAFT BOM.
testData: One ACTIVE BOM, one DRAFT BOM.
expected: Status changes to ARCHIVED. archivedAt stamped. Header and component edit controls disappear. ARCHIVED BOM is not hard-deleted.

title: Activate a BOM with no components is rejected
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. A DRAFT BOM with zero components exists.
steps:
1. Open the empty DRAFT BOM.
2. Click Activate; provide effectiveFrom date.
expected: HTTP 400: Cannot activate a BOM with no components. Status stays DRAFT.

title: BOM.VIEW-only user cannot create, edit, or activate a BOM
preconditions: A CUSTOM role with BOM.VIEW only. A DRAFT BOM exists.
steps:
1. Login as the VIEW-only user.
2. Navigate to /admin/boms.
3. Observe the create toggle and the Activate button on a DRAFT BOM detail.
expected: List renders. Create toggle is hidden (canManage() = false). On the detail, Activate, Add component, and Remove component buttons are hidden. Direct POST to create/activate returns 403.

title: BOM edit on ACTIVE BOM ignores structural fields (notes update only)
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. An ACTIVE BOM exists.
steps:
1. Open the ACTIVE BOM detail.
2. Edit notes and attempt to change outputQty.
3. Save.
testData: ACTIVE BOM. New notes. Attempted outputQty change.
expected: Notes updated. outputQty and yieldPercent are ignored on ACTIVE BOMs (service applies structural fields only when DRAFT per BR-BOM-03). UI gates structural fields behind isDraft().

title: Activate a BOM containing a structural cycle is rejected
preconditions: User has BOM.MANAGE. Product P has DRAFT BOM containing component Q; Q has ACTIVE BOM containing P.
steps: 1. Attempt to activate P's DRAFT BOM (which would create a cycle).
expected: BomCycleGuard.assertNoCycle rejects activation. HTTP 400 or appropriate error. P's BOM status stays DRAFT. No partial state change.

title: Work order list loads with status filter and pagination
preconditions: User has MANUFACTURING.VIEW. WOs in several statuses exist for the company.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/work-orders.
2. Cycle the status filter: Planned, Released, In Progress, Completed, Closed, Cancelled, All.
3. Page through.
testData: WOs in all six statuses for one company.
expected: Each filter re-queries with ?status= param and shows matching rows. Rows show WO number, FG product code/name, planned qty, status badge. Paginator shows all five controls. No uid in any visible column.

title: Create work order via product and branch pickers
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. An ACTIVE GOODS product and at least one active branch exist in the company.
steps:
1. On /admin/work-orders, open the create form.
2. Select finished product by name via picker.
3. Select branch by name via picker (non-default branch).
4. Enter plannedQty=100; optional plannedDate and notes.
5. Submit.
testData: plannedQty: 100. Branch: non-default. FG product: GOODS type.
expected: HTTP 201. Success: Work order created — {woNumber}. New row in PLANNED status. Body sent: {finishedProductUid, plannedQty:"100", branchUid}. companyId derived from JWT principal.

title: Release work order — PLANNED to RELEASED using product's ACTIVE BOM
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.RELEASE. A PLANNED WO whose FG product has an ACTIVE BOM exists.
steps:
1. Open the PLANNED WO detail.
2. Click Release (no BOM override needed).
3. Confirm.
testData: PLANNED WO. FG product with ACTIVE BOM.
expected: Status changes to RELEASED. releasedAt stamped. BOM pinned. Success: Work order released. Outbox WORK_ORDER_RELEASED emitted. No GL effect yet.

title: Release with no ACTIVE BOM is rejected
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.RELEASE. A PLANNED WO whose FG product has no ACTIVE BOM and no BOM pinned.
steps:
1. Open the PLANNED WO detail.
2. Click Release.
testData: PLANNED WO. FG product has no ACTIVE BOM.
expected: HTTP 400: No ACTIVE BOM for product {code}. Pin a BOM before releasing (BR-MFG-02). Status stays PLANNED.

title: Issue components — RELEASED to IN_PROGRESS, WIP debit accumulated
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A RELEASED WO with component products having on-hand stock and avg cost in the WO branch.
steps:
1. Open the RELEASED WO detail.
2. Set Posting date = 2026-06-14.
3. Click Issue components.
testData: postingDate: 2026-06-14. Full issue (UI always sends full:true).
expected: Status changes to IN_PROGRESS. Component lines materialised from BOM explosion and marked ISSUED/PARTIAL. PRODUCTION_ISSUE stock movements posted. WIP debit accumulated. GL DR WIP / CR Inventory. Success: Components issued.

title: Issue components with NULL avg_cost — cost-skipped, incompleteCost flag set
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A RELEASED WO with one component whose avg_cost is NULL.
steps:
1. Open the RELEASED WO.
2. Set posting date and issue components.
expected: Stock movement posted with null cost. Component line costSkipped=true. WO incompleteCost=true. No GL leg for that component (BR-MFG-06). Detail shows incomplete-cost indicator.

title: Apply labour and overhead cost — GL PRODUCTION_LABOUR posting
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A RELEASED or IN_PROGRESS WO exists.
steps:
1. Open the WO detail.
2. In Apply Cost, enter labourAmount=5000, overheadAmount=2000, postingDate=2026-06-14.
3. Submit.
expected: Labour and overhead accumulators increase. WIP debit accumulated. GL PRODUCTION_LABOUR posting created. Success: Cost applied. Posting is append-only.

title: Apply cost tied to an operation — second apply is rejected (idempotency)
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A WO with an un-applied operation exists.
steps:
1. In Apply Cost, choose an operation by description via picker.
2. Apply cost.
3. Attempt to apply cost to the same operation again.
expected: First apply marks the operation applied=true. Second apply returns 400: Operation {uid} already applied. Operation chosen by description (not uid) via picker.

title: Complete work order — IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED with FG receipt and WIP relief
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.CLOSE. An IN_PROGRESS WO with WIP accumulated. FG product is GOODS type.
steps:
1. Open the IN_PROGRESS WO detail.
2. Enter goodQty=90, scrapQty=10, postingDate=2026-06-14.
3. Submit.
expected: Status changes to COMPLETED. goodQty/scrapQty set. computedUnitCost derived from open WIP / goodQty. FG PRODUCTION_RECEIPT stock movement. GL DR Finished-Goods / CR WIP. Outbox WORK_ORDER_COMPLETED emitted.

title: Complete with goodQty exceeding plannedQty is blocked unless allowOverRun=true
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.CLOSE. An IN_PROGRESS WO with plannedQty=100.
steps:
1. Complete with goodQty=110, allowOverRun not checked.
2. Retry with the allow over-run checkbox enabled.
expected: Step 1: HTTP 400: Output (110) exceeds planned qty (100). Set allowOverRun=true to override (BR-MFG-07). Step 2: Succeeds. Exact equality (110 vs 110) is allowed.

title: Close work order — COMPLETED to CLOSED with variance cleared
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.CLOSE. A COMPLETED WO with residual WIP (rounding/variance) exists.
steps:
1. Open the COMPLETED WO detail.
2. In Close, enter postingDate=2026-06-14.
3. Submit.
expected: Status changes to CLOSED (terminal). Residual WIP cleared to Manufacturing Variance (GL PRODUCTION_VARIANCE DR/CR per sign). varianceAmount set. closedAt stamped. Success: Work order closed.

title: Cancel PLANNED work order — no stock or GL reversal needed
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A PLANNED WO exists.
steps:
1. Open the PLANNED WO detail.
2. Enter cancel reason: Customer cancelled.
3. Confirm cancel.
expected: Status changes to CANCELLED (terminal). cancelledAt stamped. No stock or GL reversal (nothing was issued). Reason is optional.

title: Cancel IN_PROGRESS work order reverses issued stock and applied labour GL
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. An IN_PROGRESS WO with issued components and applied labour/overhead exists.
steps:
1. Open the IN_PROGRESS WO detail.
2. Cancel the WO.
testData: IN_PROGRESS WO with costed issued components.
expected: Status changes to CANCELLED. Each issued component reversed via PRODUCTION_ISSUE_REVERSAL (stock restored at original value). WIP debit reversed. GL DR Inventory / CR WIP. Applied labour/overhead reversed. Reversals are append-only movements.

title: Cancel blocked for COMPLETED, CLOSED, and already-CANCELLED work orders
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. One WO in COMPLETED, one in CLOSED, one in CANCELLED.
steps:
1. Attempt cancel on the COMPLETED WO.
2. Attempt cancel on the CLOSED WO.
3. Attempt cancel on the CANCELLED WO.
testData: One WO in each terminal state.
expected: COMPLETED: HTTP 400: Cannot cancel a COMPLETED work order — close it first or contact a manager. CLOSED: HTTP 400: Cannot cancel a CLOSED work order. CANCELLED: HTTP 400: Cannot cancel a CANCELLED work order. No status change in any case.

title: WORKORDER.MANAGE without RELEASE cannot release; without CLOSE cannot complete or close
preconditions: A user with MANUFACTURING.VIEW and WORKORDER.MANAGE but NOT WORKORDER.RELEASE and NOT WORKORDER.CLOSE.
steps:
1. Login as the restricted user.
2. Open a PLANNED WO; observe Release button.
3. Open an IN_PROGRESS WO; observe Complete button.
expected: Release button hidden (canRelease() = false, as WORKORDER.RELEASE missing). Complete button hidden (canComplete() = false). Direct API calls return 403.

title: Issue components on a PLANNED (not yet released) WO is rejected
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A PLANNED WO exists.
steps:
1. Open the PLANNED WO detail.
2. Attempt to issue components.
expected: HTTP 400: Components can only be issued for RELEASED or IN_PROGRESS work orders. Status unchanged.

title: Add and remove operations on a work order
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A PLANNED or IN_PROGRESS WO exists.
steps:
1. In Add operation, enter seqNo=10, description=Cutting, workCentre=WC-1, labourAmount=100, overheadAmount=50; submit.
2. Remove the un-applied operation.
3. Attempt to remove an applied operation.
expected: Add returns 201 with operation row appended. Remove of un-applied returns 204. Remove of applied returns 400: Cannot remove an already-applied operation.

title: Work order edit allowed only while PLANNED
preconditions: User has WORKORDER.MANAGE. A PLANNED WO and a RELEASED WO exist.
steps:
1. Open the PLANNED WO; change plannedQty and branch; save.
2. Open the RELEASED WO; observe edit controls.
expected: PLANNED edit succeeds. RELEASED WO has edit controls hidden (canEdit = status PLANNED && WORKORDER.MANAGE). Direct API PUT on non-PLANNED returns 400: Work order can only be edited while PLANNED (BR-MFG-04).

title: Work order cost report screen renders planned vs actual breakdown
preconditions: User has MANUFACTURING.VIEW. A WO with issued components and applied labour/overhead exists.
steps:
1. From WO detail, navigate to the cost report route.
2. Inspect planned-vs-actual components, applied labour/overhead, WIP debit/credit, net WIP, computed unit cost, variance, incompleteCost flag.
testData: WO with costed components and applied cost.
expected: WorkOrderCostReportDto rendered. netWIP = wipDebitTotal - wipCreditTotal. Component rows show code/name. Money formatted as CUR 1,234.56. WO referenced by woNumber; uid only in URL.

title: Full happy-path work order lifecycle: PLANNED > RELEASED > IN_PROGRESS > COMPLETED > CLOSED
preconditions: ORG_ADMIN (all mfg perms). ACTIVE BOM for GOODS FG product. Component stock with avg cost in branch.
steps:
1. Create WO (PLANNED).
2. Release (RELEASED).
3. Issue components (IN_PROGRESS).
4. Apply labour=5000 and overhead=2000.
5. Complete with goodQty=90, scrapQty=10 (COMPLETED).
6. Close (CLOSED).
expected: Status badge walks PLANNED > RELEASED > IN_PROGRESS > COMPLETED > CLOSED. Final cost report shows WIP debit ≈ WIP credit, computed unit cost, residual variance cleared. FG on-hand increased by 90. All postings append-only.

title: WIP reconciliation report — balanced (ties=true)
preconditions: User has MANUFACTURING.VIEW. Company with open WOs whose WIP matches GL 1320 balance.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/manufacturing/wip-reconciliation.
2. Select the company.
3. Review the reconciliation result.
expected: WipReconciliationDto {label, computed, expected, ties=true}. ties=true rendered as balanced (no error alert). computed = Σ(wipDebit - wipCredit) of open WOs. expected = GL 1320 balance, base currency.

title: WIP reconciliation report — does not tie (ties=false) shows finance-grade defect alert
preconditions: User has MANUFACTURING.VIEW. Company where Σ open-WO WIP differs from GL 1320.
steps: 1. Open WIP reconciliation for the out-of-balance company.
testData: Company with forced WIP vs GL mismatch.
expected: ties=false. Error alert raised: WIP Reconciliation Defect — Computed WIP ({computed}) does not match GL balance ({expected}). Finance review required. Computed and expected amounts both displayed.

title: Non-manufacturing roles cannot access BOM or work order screens
preconditions: Users for ACCOUNTANT, STOREKEEPER, SALES_REP (none granted mfg/BOM perms). A NO-PERMISSION user.
steps:
1. Login as ACCOUNTANT; attempt to navigate to /admin/boms and /admin/work-orders.
2. Repeat as STOREKEEPER and SALES_REP.
3. Repeat as NO-PERMISSION user.
testData: Four user types without manufacturing permissions.
expected: Nav items Bills of Materials and Work Orders hidden for all four users. Route guards redirect to /admin/home. Direct API calls return 403 for all BOM and WO endpoints.

title: CUSTOM read-only role sees BOM and WO lists/details but cannot manage
preconditions: A CUSTOM role granted BOM.VIEW and MANUFACTURING.VIEW only.
steps:
1. Login as the read-only user.
2. Navigate to /admin/boms; verify list and detail load.
3. Observe Create, Activate, Add component buttons.
4. Navigate to /admin/work-orders; verify list and detail load.
5. Observe Create, Release, Complete, Close, Cancel buttons.
expected: BOM and WO lists and detail screens load. All create/manage/release/close/cancel buttons hidden. Direct POST/PUT to manage endpoints returns 403.
permission: BOM.VIEW + MANUFACTURING.VIEW (lacking BOM.MANAGE, WORKORDER.MANAGE, WORKORDER.RELEASE, WORKORDER.CLOSE)

title: Cross-tenant BOM and WO access denied
preconditions: ORG_ADMIN of Tenant A. BOMs/WOs in Tenant B.
steps:
1. As ORG_ADMIN of Tenant A, attempt to open a Tenant B BOM uid.
2. Attempt to open a Tenant B WO uid.
3. Attempt WO list with Tenant B companyId.
testData: Tenant B BOM uid, Tenant B WO uid, Tenant B companyId.
expected: All attempts return 403 via ScopeGuard. rootadmin can access both tenants (superuser bypass).

title: User assigned to one branch cannot create WO for an unassigned branch
preconditions: User with WORKORDER.MANAGE assigned only to Branch-1 in a multi-branch company.
steps:
1. Create a WO in Branch-1 (assigned) — succeeds.
2. Attempt to create a WO bound to Branch-2 (unassigned).
expected: Branch-1 WO creation succeeds. Branch-2 WO creation denied by ScopeGuard. Branch selected via picker by name.

title: BOM multi-level explosion API — MAKE components recursed, BUY components are leaves
preconditions: User has BOM.VIEW. A multi-level BOM exists: parent > MAKE sub-assembly > BUY raw material.
steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/boms/explode?parentProductUid={uid}&outputQty=5&multiLevel=true&withCost=false.
2. Repeat with multiLevel=false.
3. Repeat with withCost=true&branchUid={uid}.
testData: outputQty: 5. multiLevel: true then false. withCost: false then true.
expected: BomExplosionResultDto tree. MAKE components recursed down. BUY components are leaves regardless of any BOM they might have. withCost=true includes cost figures as money strings.
